image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey small PTT fuel station building, detailed front elevation with a glazed shop frontage and an attached flat forecourt canopy carried on two square clad columns, dark blue fascia band with a red lower stripe carrying the PTT wordmark and flame device, recessed downlight panels in the white canopy soffit, plain rendered side and rear walls with a service door, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: blue and red printed composite fascia panels and white perforated soffit at the front, plate glass, flat painted render on side and rear walls, galvanised roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: PTT / OR. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.84 -- not a pass self-score. 672/16000 triangles, 11/12 draw calls, 7/8 materials, 11/16 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m against the declared 8 x 4.6 x 7, with the enclosed volume at the REAR and the canopy taking the front 3.2 m.
featureReviews.notes: The setback is the whole prop: what reads as a separate awning is the building's own roof slab running forward on two columns, so the shell face is at z=0.30 rather than pushed forward like every sibling. Meshy reads the plate 43% deeper than the declared module -- the forecourt, which the plate frames as part of the object -- while agreeing on height within 4%. The kit's shared 7.0 m depth wins and the canopy is fitted inside it, so it keeps its proportion instead of being cropped. The red stripe overran to 7.01 m at its first depth and was caught by measurement, not by eye.

featureReviews.evidence: White flame glyph and italic 'ptt' on navy, right of centre on the street-facing run, with the red enamel stripe under the band on all three exposed edges.
featureReviews.notes: The band wraps three sides at ONE component and one material: the +Z run names the face that samples the canvas, the two returns are flagged plain and sample a flat corner of it. Two distinct faults had to be fixed before that held. The returns originally ran to the same depth as the front run and intersected it, smearing the canvas through the overlap; and `plain` was implemented as a sentinel slice index of -1, which still satisfied `i >= start && i < start+4` for vertices 0-2, so three corners of the +X face kept sampling the wordmark band. The test is now an explicit boolean. The flame is set as a typographic mark, not the corporate droplet -- the one part of this feature that is an approximation rather than a match.

featureReviews.evidence: 0.30 m slab reaching z=3.48, carried on two 0.34 m square columns from the ground to its soffit, in the shopfront framing material.
featureReviews.notes: The columns take the FRAME material rather than the render: in the plate they are the same clad aluminium section as the shopfront jambs. The slab is 0.30 thick, not 0.32: at 0.32 its top face sat at y=3.620 with the roof deck's top face, coplanar and co-facing over 18.6 m2.

featureReviews.evidence: One 5.20 x 2.70 m pane under the canopy, framed on four sides and divided by four mullions on a 1.05 m pitch.
featureReviews.notes: The glazing ships at #6F7477 rather than its measured #454A4B: at the measured value it composited to the harness backdrop luma of 58 and the whole shopfront was classified as an enclosed hole in the silhouette. Opacity 0.94 -- a building shell has nothing behind it, so the pane is authored as tinted and mostly opaque rather than as a window onto an empty interior.

notes: Built on the shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m building module: detailed front elevation, plain rendered side and rear walls, no loose objects outside. The attached forecourt canopy on two columns is kept because it is structural and brand-defining -- without it the building reads as a generic shop. Fuel pumps and every other loose forecourt object are excluded under the no-objects-outside rule.
